title: Scope KMS keys to region, enrich audit events, and tighten RBAC bindings for data residency
author: Priya Raman
body: Motivation: customers with strict data residency and compliance requirements have requested stronger guarantees that KMS keys and audit trails are region-scoped and that RBAC bindings prevent accidental cross-region access. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) KMS key policy scoping and an enforcement check to ensure created keys are annotated and ACL'd to a single allowed region for a tenant; 2) Audit pipeline enrichment so every audit record emitted from the control plane includes resolved region, kms_key_id (redacted for public logs), and an explicit residency_tag; 3) RBAC v2 binding templates and a migration helper that tightens previously open bindings for role principals that include 'data-residency' constraints. This is a focused compliance change that reduces blast radius for keys and makes post-hoc incident analysis much easier. What I changed (high level): - Add kms/policy/scoped_key_manager.go: enforces region annotation and rejects cross-region key reuse. - Add audit/enrich/region_enricher.go and schema v2 bump with a backwards-compatible field (residency_tag) and migration guidance. - Add rbac/v2/templates/data_residency_bindings.yaml and generator script rbac/tools/generate_residency_bindings.go to produce tightened bindings from existing role manifests. - Integration tests under infra/tests/kms_region_scope_integration_test.go that run in CI with simulated tenant metadata. - Add migration script tools/migrations/20260222_migrate_residency_bindings.sh and docs/compliance/kms-region-scoping.md. Rollout plan: staged feature flag rollout per-tenant (feature.flag.kms_region_scoping) with safety switch to opt-out for SE-assisted migrations. Also included a small admin console notice for affected tenants. Checklist: - [x] KMS enforcement code and unit tests - [x] Audit enrichment + schema bump + compatibility note - [x] RBAC generator + tests - [x] Migration script and manual rollback steps - [x] CI green on linux/amd64 integration suite - [x] Documentation updates and release notes Notes: this PR intentionally does not auto-block existing keys; instead we emit a warning and provide a migration helper that rotates or re-creates keys in-region. The audit schema bump is additive and backwards compatible; downstream consumers should start consuming residency_tag when available. Related: Linear ENG-2987 (data residency enforcement), SEC-412 (kms scoping threat model), SUP-1023 (customer support case about cross-region key leak).

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can you clarify whether the scoped_key_manager rejects keys missing the region tag or only flags them? Right now behavior looks like 'reject' in code but docs say 'warn'.

Priya Raman (author): Good catch — updated with explicit preflight: newly created keys are rejected if no region tag is present; existing keys are only warned and flagged for migration. Added comment and test to assert this behavior.
Rui Zhang: Audit schema bump looks additive which is great. Please ensure consumer teams are pinged; added a TODO to the release checklist to send a migration email to the observability consumers.
Priya Raman: Added note in docs/compliance and configured a one-time alert for downstream consumers in the release playbook.
Claire Nguyen: RBAC generator LGTM but we need an idempotency test for existing bindings so we don't create duplicates during migration runs.
Priya Raman: Added idempotency checks and a small dedupe step in generate_residency_bindings.go; included unit test.
merge: squash and merge by Ethan Cole. Final merge commit message: 'Scope KMS keys to region, audit enrichment, RBAC residency bindings — ENH:ENG-2987 SEC-412'
release_notes: Add region-scoped KMS key enforcement (opt-in per-tenant via feature flag), audit event enrichment with residency_tag and kms_key_id (redacted), and RBAC v2 templates to tighten bindings for data residency. Includes migration helpers and operator guidance.
summary: Implements KMS region scoping, audit schema enrichment, and RBAC binding tightening to support customer data residency/compliance requirements.
